newsitem.title: Belgium: FULL TEXT - KREDIETBANK H1 96 EARNINGS STATEMENT.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - KREDIETBANK H1 96 EARNINGS STATEMENT.

text.p: Following is the full text of a statement released by Kredietbank .
The Kredietbank posts further growth of activities and results
At BEF 6 688 million, the consolidated profit of the Kredietbank for the first six months of 1996 was 14.5 % up on the figure for the corresponding period of 1995.

This favourable development was due principally to the good results posted by the professional and international activities. The first half of 1996 also saw the acquisition of the Bank van Roeselare already making a positive contribution to consolidated profit.
On the basis of current forecasts and provided no unforeseen circumstances arise, profit is expected to follow a positive trend during the second half.
Consolidated balance sheet

As at 30 June 1996, the consolidated balance sheet total amounted to BEF 3 510 billion, an increase of BEF 548 billion or 18.5 % on the figure as at 30 June 1995. Excluding the effect of the acquisition of the Bank van Roeselare, the increase would still have been above 15 %.
The growth was due primarily to the expansion of international activities, external assets rising by 23 %.
There was further strong expansion of interbank activities. Loans and advances to credit institutions rose by 16.6 % and amounts owed to credit institutions by 18.4 %.

Customers' deposits and debts represented by securities totalled BEF 1 842 billion; a rise of BEF 281 billion or 18 % on the figure as at 30 June 1995. Savings deposits climbed to above BEF 377 billion, a rise of 29.1 % or BEF 47 billion since 1 January 1996.

The total amount of credit outstanding went up by 22.8 %, international lending being particularly buoyant. Domestic lending expanded at a somewhat slower rate, although home loans registered a rise of 14.8 %.
The securities portfolio grew by 16.4 % and as at the end of June 1996 amounted to BEF 984 billion, the rise being due principally to investment in government funds and government paper (+ 22,3 %).
Own funds in the narrow sense rose by 9.8 % to BEF 94 billion. Capital resources (own funds + the fund for general banking risks + subordinated loans) totalled BEF 222 billion.
At 10.7 %, the overall risk asset ratio was substantially above the norm of 8 % set by the supervisory bodies.
Consolidated results

For the first half of the year, current gross income was 24.1 % up on its level for the first six months of 1995. Interest earnings rose by 13.4 %, due chiefly to the growth of foreign lending. Earnings from financial transactions climbed by 80,8 %, thanks mainly to the very good results on professional exchange and trading activities. Other commission and operating income also made more than satisfactory progress (up 38.6 %), the result of primarily the favourable trend of BEVEK and SICAV placements. Notable in this respect was the success of the issues with guaranteed repayment, in respect of which the Kredietbank is building itself up as a market leader.

Virtually half of the 8.9 % increase in operating costs was due to the inclusion of the Bank van Roeselare in the consolidation, the rest being accounted for by the foreign branches and the foreign and professional subsidiaries; this was in line with the further expansion of international and professional activities.

Total depreciation, write-downs and provisions in the profit and loss account posted a rise of BEF 3 732 million to BEF 7 872 million on their level for the first six months of 1995. The sharp increase of depreciation on fixed assets had chiefly to do with the acquisition of the Bank van Roeselare and substantial investment in fixed assets.

Write-downs and provisions for credit risks were up on their level for the corresponding half of 1995 by BEF 1 519 million to BEF 3 782 million. The rise in write-downs on receivables was situated mainly in foreign lending and was limited, the loss percentage remaining low. Write-downs on domestic lending began to stabilize and the overall increase for write-downs and provisions for credit risks was consequently due principally to higher allocations to the internal reserve for latent risks.

On balance, allocations to provisions for credit risks and costs amounted to BEF 1 952 million. Substantial provisions were set side for the costs that will be incurred in respect of the introduction of the "Euro", the adjustment of information technology to the switchover to the year 2000, the integration of HSA/Spaarkrediet information technology and the further automation of the branch network.
Income tax rose by BEF 1 531 million to BEF 3 992 million, or by 62.2 %.
Net profit, after deduction of minority interests, went up from BEF 5 843 million for the first half of 1995 to BEF 6 688 million for the corresponding period of 1996.
Non-consolidated annual accounts

At Kredietbank NV level, the growth of most balance sheet and profit and loss account components was slightly less than at the consolidated level, where the Bank van Roeselare was included in the consolidation for the first time.
In respect of the first six months of 1995, there was a 16.3 % rise in lending, and customers' deposits and debts represented by securities climbed by 14.9 %.
Gross income was up by 20.3 % and operating costs by 3.6 %.
Net profit rose by 10.1 % to BEF 4 764 million on its level for the corresponding period of last year.
